account:
Today seems mostly routine so far. I attended the morning market walk and am now home for the noon lunch appointment, before town accounts at one. Residents have repeated reports of the baker carrying wheat at the bakery and a sack of bread at the inn. I saw the baker stock the market chest, bought two fresh loaves, and heard the baker report thirty-two fresh loaves stocked and no town problem. This looks consistent with ordinary bread production and distribution; I have no evidence of anything improper or unusual behind it.

The builder wants a paid repair commission and needs specific locations, standards, and an approved price. I asked for an inspection and itemized estimate before authorizing paid work. My later instruction specifying a bridge inspection and a one-o'clock report was not heard, so I should not assume the builder knows that arrangement. No construction or payment has been authorized.

The unresolved issue is my three-o'clock tea appointment: the book says a neighbour at a dockside cottage on the east bank, but supplies neither a name nor a specific cottage. The secretary said she would confirm the address. I also asked market residents and the baker, but have heard no answer identifying the host. It may simply be an incomplete appointment entry; I have no basis for attributing any other purpose to it. I should check with the secretary at accounts and keep the afternoon appointments.
